title: Drift: firmware forensics for science
pitch: Consumer wearables are used as research instruments, and vendors silently change their step, heart-rate and sleep algorithms in firmware updates, which makes cohort data from before and after an update non-comparable. Drift takes two or more firmware versions of an open-source wearable, finds the code on the metric path, runs each version's algorithm on the same recorded sensor data so the effect is a measured number, and writes a dated data-validity memo for a research team.
how_it_works: Take two or more firmware versions of an open-source wearable (Bangle.js / Espruino, PineTime / InfiniTime). The firmware is open source; the recordings are third-party data that are fetched from their owners, cited and never redistributed.
Locate the code on the metric path, from sensor input to reported metric, and show what changed.
Run differential execution: compile the metric algorithm from each version for the host and feed every version the same recorded raw sensor data.
Write a dated memo for the research team: which date ranges are not comparable, by how much, and a suggested sensitivity check.

boundaries.title: 2v09 to 2v10: from a simple threshold counter to a filtered, gated counter
boundaries.summary: Before, a step was counted whenever the squared acceleration magnitude dipped below 1 g minus 80 counts and then rose above 1 g plus 80 counts. From 2v10 on, the magnitude is first passed through a 57-tap band-pass filter that keeps roughly 1.3 to 2.5 Hz (typical walking cadence), and a step is a swing from below to above a threshold in the filtered signal. A step is only counted if the step five steps earlier happened less than 75 samples (6 seconds) ago, so isolated movements stop counting.
changes: inline hysteresis on |a|^2 replaced by a 57-tap band-pass FIR on |a|
threshold crossing in the filtered signal instead of raw magnitude
a history gate: 5 steps within 75 samples before steps count (the steps that opened the gate are not credited)
boundaries.expected_effect: far fewer counts when the wearer is not walking, and a different bias when walking
boundaries.authored_by: Claude, from the code diff (git diff of libs/misc/stepcount.c between the commits each generation builds from; 2v09 is read from RELEASE_2V09:libs/banglejs/jswrap_bangle.c). Plain-language reading, not upstream documentation.

boundaries.title: 2v10 to 2v11: a short filter, peak detection and a step-timing state machine
boundaries.summary: The 57-tap filter and the fixed threshold are gone. The signal goes through a 7-tap filter, a step is a local peak in the filtered signal, and a small state machine accepts a step only if it follows the previous one after 4 to 16 samples (about 0.33 to 1.3 s). Six accepted steps in a row start the count, and those six are then credited at once, so steps are no longer lost at the start of each walk. A raw-signal gate additionally keeps the counter closed unless the unfiltered signal has moved by more than 14 units (of 32 counts) for 3 samples.
changes: peak detection and a state machine with 4 to 16 sample step spacing and 6 steps in a row
retroactive credit of the first steps of a run
boundaries.expected_effect: the largest behaviour change in the lineage: fewer non-walking counts again, different bias on slow or irregular walking
boundaries.authored_by: Claude, from the code diff (git diff of libs/misc/stepcount.c between the commits each generation builds from; 2v09 is read from RELEASE_2V09:libs/banglejs/jswrap_bangle.c). Plain-language reading, not upstream documentation.

boundaries.title: 2v11 to 2v12: a moving DC offset instead of a fixed 1 g
boundaries.summary: The magnitude used to be shifted by a fixed 8192 counts (1 g). It now subtracts an exponential moving average of the magnitude (a time constant of 12 samples, about one second), so slow changes in orientation or gravity no longer leak into the signal. The raw gate threshold goes from 14 to 15. The square-root helper moves into a shared header with no change in behaviour.
changes: exponential moving-average DC removal (alpha 1/12) replacing the fixed 8192 offset
int_sqrt32 moved to jsutils.h (no behaviour change)
boundaries.expected_effect: small change in walking bias, further reduction in counts while the wrist is still but tilting
boundaries.authored_by: Claude, from the code diff (git diff of libs/misc/stepcount.c between the commits each generation builds from; 2v09 is read from RELEASE_2V09:libs/banglejs/jswrap_bangle.c). Plain-language reading, not upstream documentation.

boundaries.title: 2v12-2v21 to 2v22-2v28: cosmetic
boundaries.summary: Only the order of the keywords in one declaration (static const) and a whitespace change. The compiled behaviour is the same, and Drift's null control confirms identical counts and step events on every recording.
boundaries.authored_by: Claude, from the code diff (git diff of libs/misc/stepcount.c between the commits each generation builds from; 2v09 is read from RELEASE_2V09:libs/banglejs/jswrap_bangle.c). Plain-language reading, not upstream documentation.

boundaries.title: 2v22-2v28 to 2v29: a clamp bug fix on an unreachable line
boundaries.summary: When the filter output fell below -32768 the old code set it to +32768 instead of -32768. The fix corrects the sign. With the 7-tap filter the output is bounded by about 6,700 in magnitude (inputs are clipped to -128..127 and the taps sum to 208 in absolute value, shifted right by 2), so the line cannot be reached. Counts and step events are identical on all 126 recordings, and Drift treats this release as a second null control.
boundaries.authored_by: Claude, from the code diff (git diff of libs/misc/stepcount.c between the commits each generation builds from; 2v09 is read from RELEASE_2V09:libs/banglejs/jswrap_bangle.c). Plain-language reading, not upstream documentation.

same_walk.note: one recorded 10,021-step walk, counted by each generation (no tail flush)

native_walk_check.definition: per-file shift = error(b) - error(a), percentage points of the file's expected total; the six labelled HughB walking files (one wearer), replayed natively at 12.5 Hz; no CI

resampler_sensitivity.note: Same firmware and recordings, only the 15 -> 12.5 Hz resampler changes (poly is Drift's default).  Medians for the semi-regular and irregular gaits and the boundary CIs depend on it.

caveats: Drift replays the step-counting algorithm only. Sensor-driver, sampling or settings changes in a firmware release cannot be reproduced from recordings.
Release dates are the commit dates of the git release tags. A watch runs a version only after its owner installs it, so a participant's real switch date is later and unknown without logs.

Clemson subjects are 30 adults aged 19 to 27 walking marked courses; the Bangle.js recordings come from a few wearers (mostly one) and their expected totals are taken from file names and upstream main.c (provenance undocumented). Neither is an older-adult cohort.

The Clemson-to-Bangle.js transfer is unvalidated: on the six native Bangle.js walking recordings (one wearer, no resampling) the boundary shifts disagree with the Clemson shifts (see native_walk_check). Verdicts that Clemson calls comparable but the native walks contradict are reported as 'not confirmed'.

Clemson data (15 Hz, g) is resampled to the device's 12.5 Hz and 8192 counts per g (polyphase 5/6) and saturated to int16; this adapter is Drift's, not the device's. Count-error medians for the semi-regular and irregular gaits and the boundary CIs depend on the resampler (see resampler_sensitivity: linear interpolation gives materially different numbers). The Clemson wrist sensor recorded only -2 to +2 g, so strong peaks are clipped.

A 'comparable' verdict means the 95% bootstrap CI of the MEAN paired shift lies within +-2 points. Individual participants can still change by more (sd_pct, n_beyond_threshold and max_abs_subject_change_pct are reported), 6 pairs x 4 gaits are examined without multiplicity correction, and the margin is a convention.
Confidence intervals are bootstrap intervals over subjects (10,000 resamples, seed 42); they describe between-subject variation, not population mismatch.

Per-step F1 is only meaningful against its reference rows: in Regular gait a +-250 ms window spans ~94% of the median 0.53 s step interval, so random timing and an oracle metronome are reported beside the firmware. +-500 ms is not reported.
The per-step alignment value (latency_s) is a phase, not a device latency: gait is periodic, so it is identified only modulo the step period (~0.5 to 0.6 s).
False-positive rates rest on 5 drive/train files from one wearer (2.4 h in total, timestamp span) and have no confidence interval.
The plain-language description of each firmware change is written by Claude from the code diff.
